recipes.name: Scrumptious Sauerkraut Balls
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can sauerkraut, well drained and finely chopped
2 tablespoons Italian seasoned dry bread crumbs
0.75 cup Italian seasoned dry bread crumbs
1 quart vegetable oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir sausage and onion in the hot skillet until sausage is crumbly and browned, about 10 minutes. Drain grease and allow to cool slightly.

Transfer sausage mixture into a large bowl. Stir in drained sauerkraut, 2 tablespoons bread crumbs, mustard, garlic salt, and pepper. Combine cream cheese and parsley in a small bowl; mix into sauerkraut mixture. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Place flour into a shallow bowl. Whisk together egg and milk in another bowl. Place 3/4 cup bread crumbs in a third bowl.
Heat oil in a deep fryer to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Shape sauerkraut mixture into 3/4-inch balls. Coat balls in flour, then dip in egg mixture and roll in bread crumbs to thoroughly coat.
Working in batches, fry balls in hot oil until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Scrumptious Sauerkraut Balls
raw_recipe.description: These sauerkraut balls are made with pork sausage and sauerkraut blended with herb cream cheese, coated in bread crumbs, then deep-fried until crisp.

review.reviewBody: These can be baked in a 350 degree oven for 20 minutes instead of frying. they freeze well. My family favorite.

We loved this. Actually, I made a mistake when making it, and added the whole pack of cream cheese. (8oz) The meatballs turned out more like a patty, but they were great tasting. I baked them at 350 for 35 minutes on a greased cookie sheet, flipping them all once 1/2 way through. I might try them with chopped up chicken next time, as they resemble the taste of chicken croquettes or even crab cakes.
Awesome recipe. I use a 1/8 measuring cup to have a consistent-sized ball. With that, I end up with 30 sauerkraut balls all exact size. I baked mine at 375 for 13 minutes. This is a party favorite!

Great recipe! My family and friends have told me they are better than the German restaurants we have around town. I followed the recipe to exact portions. After a couple of times I added some more onions. Instead of 1/4 cup of chopped onions, I use 1/2 cup of onions. I also add more flour and bread crumbs to roll them in. Last night my grandson wanted to add a little horseradish to the balls after they’re cooked. Not bad at all, just beware to add a little at a time for your taste.

I have made theses for years.. they are delicious hot and cold. I do add a whole block of cream cheese and you have to use a good dry ground mustard I use about half a bottle I taste as I go till its perfect and tangy. Its best with Jimmy deans hot sausage but all will work. I also spread out along the mixing bowl I use and put in the freezer till it stiffen a little sonics easy to ball up. Hope this helps with what the problems ive seen people comment.. they are delicious I like to make little tiny ones my husband likes golf ball size so I make a mix of all sizes. Never baked always fried them

These are delicious and have been a hit in my house over and over again. I use Italian ground sausage and follow the recipe exactly. Just a trick I have found. Really squeeze the juice out of the sauerkraut. I drain it, then hand squeeze it then pat it dry with a paper towel. The balls stay put together that way. I have also froze them and they turned out great.

These are delicious! I did use homemade rye bread crumbs instead of Italian bread crumbs as I had a 2 day old lord af of rye on hand. Also, used an airfryer to cook. They turned out great. Will make again.
Made with spicy sausage and baked in oven. They were amazing! Will make these again!

I used hot breakfast sausage, stone ground mustard, gluten free bread crumbs and flour. We served them with hot sauce, stone ground Dijon mustard and ranch (for those with a sensitive pallet). Everyone loved them so much ... I made a double batch for Christmas Eve party. We call them dragon balls because of the added heat.
I used left over Hungarian sausage that I ground myself. I also used a full 8oz of cream cheese.

If there were 10 stars, I would give it 10 stars. Made as is. Do not have a deep fryer so I browned in about an inch of oil in a frying pan then baked about 10 minutes in a 375 degree oven. Drained on paper towels and yes, they live up to the “scrumptious” title!! Thank you!!
Taste just like the kraut balls from my favorite German restaurant! I pair them with either spicy brown mustard or German mustard. Delicious!!!
Pretty good. But not great. You need to add more binding agents. They fall apart. This made about 20.
Made them for New Years! Great flavor and perfect with pork.
Made pretty much as is, little more sauerkraut, lots more bread crumbs. Eded up with 24 balls cutting the recipe in half. Baked them.
Made with goetta. Very tasty but labor intensive on the stove. I’ll bake or air fry next time. Great recipe!
These taste great and I am ask to Make again and again
The only thing I changed, was that I baked them. Next time I will try cooking them in the Air Fryer. They were really good!
These are absolutely delicious. Even without dipping in mustard!
Love this recipe!
